extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/agents/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner procedures governing filing dates, completeness, conversion, and missing parts for U.S. provisional, nonprovisional, and design patent applications. Covers when filing dates are accorded, required elements (claims, drawings, specification), notices, petitions, fees, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing date rule (post-Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed on or after December 18, 2013 will be given a filing date as of the date a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013 are dated under pre-PLT (AIA) 37 CFR 1.53(c) (written description and any necessary drawings). Amendments (other than those required to make the provisional comply with regulations) are not permitted after the provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit missing elements (37 CFR 1.53(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification or drawing are omitted, 37 CFR 1.53(e) requires that the applicant be notified and given a time period in which to submit the missing element to complete the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 601.01(f)/(g) for treatment of applications filed without drawings or without all figures. OPAP mails notices (e.g., Notice of Omitted Items or Notice of Incomplete Application) requiring reply within set periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet / application data sheet requirement for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(c)(1) requires all provisional applications be filed with a cover sheet, which may be an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or a cover letter identifying the application as a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is not clearly identified as provisional it will be treated under 37 CFR 1.53(b). A provisional identified as such but lacking a complete cover sheet under 37 CFR 1.51(c)(1) will still be treated as provisional but must submit the complete cover sheet and a surcharge later in conformance with 37 CFR 1.53(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing cover sheet or fee — notification and time to supply (usually two months)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a provisional application does not have a complete cover sheet or the appropriate fee, the applicant will be notified pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(g) and given a time period (usually two months) to provide the necessary fee or cover sheet and to pay the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(g) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If filing fee not timely paid, the Office may dispose of the provisional application. If no correspondence address provided, applicant has two months from filing date to file basic filing fee, cover sheet, and pay surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of provisional applications available upon request/fee unless disposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of a provisional application will be provided by the USPTO upon request and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.19(b) unless the provisional application has been disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposition includes abandonment or other removal from USPTO files (see 37 CFR 1.53(e) and (g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee requirement for provisional when later claiming 35 U.S.C.119(e) benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic filing fee must be paid in a provisional application on filing or within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(g) if any claim for benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) based on that application is made in a subsequently filed nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.78 for benefit-claiming procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to review refusal to accord filing date (37 CFR 1.53(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(e)(2) requires any request for review of a refusal to accord an application a filing date be made by way of a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must include required evidence; see MPEP § 506.02 for petition practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from nonprovisional to provisional (37 CFR 1.53(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraph (b) may be converted to a provisional application and be accorded the original filing date of the application filed under paragraph (b) if a request for conversion is filed with the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(q)) prior to abandonment, payment of the issue fee, or 12 months after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for conversion must include processing fee; grant does not entitle applicant to refund of fees paid in original application. Provisional filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(d)) and surcharge (1.16(g)) are required for the provisional application (may be paid later after Notice to File Missing Parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from nonprovisional to provisional does not necessarily avoid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting a nonprovisional application to a provisional application will not avoid the publication of the nonprovisional application unless the request to convert is recognized in sufficient time to permit removal from the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot ensure removal from publication after the publication process has been initiated. For procedures see MPEP § 1120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application cannot claim priority/benefit after conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is not entitled to claim priority to or benefit of a prior-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 119, 120, 121, 365, or 386. After conversion of a nonprovisional to provisional, any priority or benefit claims submitted in the nonprovisional will be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of loss of priority/benefit rights when converting to provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from provisional to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.53(c)(3)) — requirements and patent-term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional and accorded the original provisional filing date, but the request must be accompanied by the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(i) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (unless the provisional already contains such a claim). The nonprovisional must include filing/search/exam fees and possible surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion will not refund provisional fees and can adversely affect patent term (the patent term will be measured from at least the provisional filing date). Applicants should consider claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead of conversion to avoid adverse patent term and be less expensive. Requests to convert must be filed prior to abandonment of the provisional or expiration of 12 months after the provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing designation for mailed conversion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who wish to file a request for conversion by mail should designate 'Mail Stop Conversion' as part of the USPTO address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to conversion both directions per relevant paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP review for applications filed without all pages of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP reviews application papers to determine whether all pages of specification are present. If an application filed without all pages nonetheless contains something that can be construed as a written description (and required figures/claims where applicable), OPAP will send a Notice of Omitted Items indicating a filing date was accorded but pages are lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application contains nothing that can be construed as a written description, OPAP will mail a Notice of Incomplete Application indicating no filing date is granted (lack of 35 U.S.C. 112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Options when an application is missing page(s) but is entitled to a filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: After an OPAP notice, the applicant may (A) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with evidence of deposit (petition fee refundable if page(s) shown received), (B) submit omitted page(s) and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the later filing date (two-month period, extendable under 1.136), or (C) accept the application as deposited by filing an appropriate amendment (e.g., substitute specification renumbering pages and cancelling incomplete sentences) without adding new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For option B, filing omitted pages and requesting the later filing date is tantamount to filing a new application; applicants should consider filing a new application as a cost-effective alternative. If omitted portion is fully contained in a prior-filed application, amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b) may be used to include it (must comply with 1.57(b) and 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO will not grant petitions to accept omitted pages in provisional applications — file new provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not grant petitions under 37 CFR 1.182 to accept omitted page(s) and accord an application filing date as of the date of such submission in provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should file a new completed provisional application instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: If application not entitled to filing date — applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: If OPAP mails a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' (no filing date), applicant may (A) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with fee and evidence asserting missing specification was submitted or that deposited papers contain adequate written description, (B) submit the omitted specification including at least one claim (if required) and accept the date of such submission as the filing date, or (C) submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b) in a nonprovisional application (if specification is completely contained in prior-filed application) accompanied by a petition under 1.53(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month periods are extendable under 37 CFR 1.136; petitions must include sufficient evidence (37 CFR 1.181(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling when forwarded to Technology Center missing pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application forwarded for examination lacks pages of the specification and no OPAP Notice of Omitted Items was mailed, the examiner should determine whether the application is entitled to a filing date and, if entitled, notify applicant in the next Office action to either accept the application as filed, file omitted pages with a petition under 1.182, or file a petition under 1.53(e) alleging deposit with supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition filed will be forwarded to the Office of Petitions. If examiner determines application is not entitled to a filing date, forward application to OPAP for mailing of a 'Notice of Incomplete Application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application filed without at least one claim (pre-Dec 18, 2013 and design apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013 or design applications, a claim is a statutory requirement for according a filing date. If no claim is present, a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' is mailed indicating no filing date; the filing date becomes the date of receipt of at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain alternatives exist (e.g., petition to convert to 35 U.S.C. 111(b) under 37 CFR 1.53(c)(2) where conversion before 12 months may avoid the claim requirement). Preliminary amendments cancelling all claims without new or substitute claims will be disapproved but won't cause denial of filing date; for fee purposes the Office treats such an application as containing a single claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed without drawings — filing date and necessity analysis (35 U.S.C. 113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design applications and pre-Dec 18, 2013 applications must have required drawings (where necessary for understanding under 35 U.S.C. 113) to receive a filing date. For other applications filed on or after December 18, 2013, drawings are not required for a filing date but should be submitted if necessary for understanding because amendments cannot introduce new matter after filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed without drawings are inspected to determine whether a drawing is referred to in the specification and whether a drawing is necessary for understanding. If drawings are necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 and missing, OPAP will mail a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' and the application may be returned to OPAP. If drawings are not necessary, the application may be processed without them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter categories where drawings usually not necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO practice treats applications with at least one process/method claim or certain composition applications as not usually requiring drawings. Examples where drawings usually not considered necessary include coated articles/products, articles made from a particular material or composition, laminated structures (unless significant structure), and articles where the sole distinguishing feature is presence of a particular material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application directed to such subject matter does describe drawing figures in the specification but was filed without drawings, it will be treated as filed without all drawing figures referred to in the specification (MPEP § 601.01(g)), provided the application contains something that can be construed as a written description.
